transcript: Last night my friend Tony and I went to Solo, a theatrical comedy show written and performed by Gabe Mollica. The main themes of the show are friendships and relationships but it covers a lot of ground. Other topics include Stephen Sondheim, straight men, and summer camp. Gabe's storytelling is somewhat akin to that of Mike Birbiglia or Alex Edelman. The jokes are current, the stories are engaging and funny, and Gabe's presence is earnest and endearing. I was also impressed by the way the show is structured — there are times where Gabe recycles or calls back to earlier jokes in really clever ways, almost like motifs, which adds a cool type of theatricality and structure to it that you don't really get with your everyday comedy show. Solo is currently running at the Connolly Theater's upstairs space in the East Village so don't miss it. With that, another program for my collection.
